Floor holds at 26; the entire blend + trip-test residual is now pinned to one global.c allocation-order fact (px pri 32727 vs g_src pri 30000) with the exact flip arithmetic derived, and five structur

frontier.hypothesis: px is seated on the target's $a0 exactly when g_src's global.c priority exceeds px's 32727, or px's drops below g_src's 30000; with the incumbent's nrefs of 12 each that means g_src at live_length <= 10, or px at live_length >= 13.
frontier.mechanism: global.c:635-653 orders allocnos by nrefs*30000/live_length and hands each the lowest free non-conflicting hard register; $v0 is blocked for px by p118 (count - 1, pri 90000). If g_src is allocated first it takes $v1 and px falls to $a0; if px falls below 30000 it lands at 27692, ties r_src, wins the tie on ascending pseudo number (122 < 123, global.c:652-653), and the order becomes g_src, px, r_src -> $v1, $a0, $a1, which is the target exactly.
frontier.next_probe: Attack live_length rather than reference count - s14 proved reference count is immovable here (Q1's extra reference is refolded by combine; s13's D2/D3 are worse). g_src's range runs from its andi (row 100) to the g sum (row 114) and needs to lose 2. Read tmp/grind/func_8003DE14/s14/d_aac/code6cac_c2.sched and .lreg for the exact LUIDs of g_src's birth and death insns, then ask tools/sched_solver (order- and clock-exact for this pass) whether a two-slot lift of the g sum is reachable WITHOUT moving the r sum, before spelling any more C.

frontier.hypothesis: The residual rows that would survive the px/g_src swap - the three channel sums, the b source register and the trip test - are all one local-alloc coalescing decision: our build merges a dying source quantity with its destination quantity where the target keeps two quantities.
frontier.mechanism: local-alloc (local-alloc.c combine_regs / qty preference, instrumented at local-alloc.c:1437, 1518, 2215) ties a destination quantity to a source quantity that dies in the same insn, which is why our sums overwrite an operand ($a1, $a0, $v1) instead of landing in the scratch $v0 the target uses at rows 111/114/118. Local-alloc runs before global-alloc and its choices are hard conflicts, so this also feeds back into the px seat.
frontier.next_probe: Run BB2_QTY_DEBUG=1 and BB2_SUGG_DEBUG=1 on the candidate chassis (tmp/grind/func_8003DE14/s14/dump.sh takes ENVVAR=1 arguments) and read which quantities local-alloc combines in the blend arm and what suggestion drives each. Do NOT spell a shared sum variable - s14 measured that at 53. The question the dump must answer is whether the coalescing is suggestion-driven (and therefore steerable by which value dies where) or unconditional.

frontier.hypothesis: The 4-insn head residual (the blez delay slot, target row 70 'move t4,zero' vs our 'addiu a2,sp,1040') is still open and is independent of the blend arm.
frontier.mechanism: reorg.c fills the guard branch's delay slot with the closest movable preceding insn; the spellings that hand it j = 0 are exactly the ones that lose the j/complement $t4/$t5 seat (measured in s12 and again in s13 E1-E6).
frontier.next_probe: Unchanged from s13: on the E1 chassis (j = 0 first, score 30) dump BB2_ALLOC_DEBUG and read the exact nrefs/livelen pair for the j and complement pseudos so the required delta is known rather than guessed, then look for an ordinary-C spelling that changes reg_n_refs of one of them by one without changing the emitted insns.
